narrative.title: Measuring the Roundabout's Circumference
narrative.scenario: A plant's transport chain has a suspected roundabout — a section that cycles back onto itself. Control wants the number of stations trapped inside the cycling section, not just whether it exists. The two-speed probe rig confirms the loop and parks both probes at a meeting station; one probe then walks the roundabout exactly once, counting stations until it returns to that parking spot.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of N node values and an integer C — the 1-based position of the node the tail connects to for the loop, or 0 when there is no loop.
narrative.outputFormat: The number of nodes inside the loop, or 0 when the list has no loop.

testCases.explanation: The tail reconnects to the 4th node (33); the roundabout 33-10-21-39-90-58-45 holds seven stations.
Both nodes sit inside the loop, so the circumference is the whole list.

hintLevels: Level 1: Detect first, measure second — a loop with zero stations is no loop at all.
Level 2: After the probes meet, park a counter at 1, advance one probe, and stop when it arrives back at the meeting station.
Level 3: The count starts at 1 because the meeting station itself is part of the loop — counting only the steps after it would under-report by exactly one.
